ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in $\triangle ABC$, $\angle ACB = 90^\circ$, CE is the angle bisector of $\triangle ABC$, and $\angle AEC = 105^\circ$. What is the measure of $\angle B$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Given that $\angle ACB=90^\circ$ and CE is the angle bisector of $\triangle ABC$, \\
it follows that $\angle ACE=\angle BCE=45^\circ$,\\
Furthermore, since $\angle AEC=105^\circ$,\\
it results in $\angle B=\angle AEC-\angle BCE=105^\circ-45^\circ=\boxed{60^\circ}$.

From the text, angle ACB is 90 degrees, CE bisects the angle at C, and angle AEC is 105 degrees. Since CE bisects the right angle at C, angle BCE is 45 degrees. In triangle CEB, angle AEC is the exterior angle at E because A, E, B are collinear in the image. Use the exterior angle theorem: angle AEC = angle B + angle BCE. Therefore angle B = 105 - 45 = 60 degrees.
